key_insight: Circulating CD14+ monocytes show glioma-specific transcriptional changes that can be used by a machine learning model to detect glioma and monitor recurrence from blood.
clinical_relevance: This suggests a non-invasive blood-based tool could complement MRI and biopsy for glioma detection, postoperative surveillance, and prognosis.
method: Single-cell RNA sequencing of blood immune cells to identify glioma-related monocyte signatures
Built an ensemble machine learning model from CD14+ monocyte transcriptomic profiles
Validated performance in independent cohorts and postoperative recurrence samples
evidence_signal: The model achieved mean cross-validation AUC 0.975 in training, AUC 0.888 in an independent cohort of 567 participants, and recurrence detection AUC 0.975 in 51 postoperative samples.
watch_item: Results are promising but need broader external validation and real-world testing before routine clinical use, especially across tumor subtypes and treatment settings.
paper_title: Sensitive Glioma Detection and Recurrence Monitoring Using a Machine Learning Model Based on Circulating Monocytes
